# The results page and search features

Google described its results page as an auction in which results of different types compete for space (a metaphor, said at the event), with text results the most common type. Query understanding decides which result types appear: explicit words such as 'pictures' signal the intent, and for ambiguous queries Google uses historical interaction data. A text result has an attribution (site name, favicon, URL), a title link and a snippet, which Google generates from its understanding of the page, and Google can add badges such as a preferred-source badge. Search features are built as the last serving step, after ranking, and most need nothing from the site owner; rich results are the exception that relies on structured data. Images appear among web results because, Google said, people began adding words such as 'pictures' to queries in 2005-2006, which led to universal search in May 2007 (said at the event); those image results come from Google's image index, and video results take thumbnails and attribution from the page or its markup. The site name is an attribution feature that owners can influence with WebSite markup on the home page. This extends Day 2: feature extraction pulls structured data, images and videos from the page during indexing, and snippets are rebuilt from the stored tokens (said at the event). Day 1's second recording added that after ordering the results Google constructs the page by deciding which search features fit the query's intent, that a majority of search features now use AI (said at the event), and that ads in Search are clearly marked as sponsored. Google's site names, introduced on mobile for select languages in October 2022, became available in all languages in September 2023.

Based on: `D3-C302`, `D3-C303`, `D3-C304`, `D3-C305`, `D3-C309`, `D3-C314`, `D3-C315`, `D3-C316`, `D3-C317`, `D3-C322`, `D3-C323`, `D3-C324`, `D3-C306`, `D3-C307`, `D3-C319`, `D3-C320`, `D3-C335`, `D3-C336`, `D2-C446`, `D2-C724`, `D1-C222`, `D1-C223`, `D1-C144`, `D2-C980`.

## Shown and said at the event

- **[Stage]** Ads in Google Search are clearly marked as sponsored.
  <br><sub>`D1-C144` · Day 1, Welcome and opening keynotes (speaker not identified) · consistent with Google docs · [How ads work on Google Search](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/our-approach/ads-on-search/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** After ordering the results, Google constructs the results page by deciding which search features fit the intent of the query.
  <br><sub>`D1-C222` · Day 1, How Search works and where's AI? (Cherry Prommawin) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said a majority of its search features now use AI.
  <br><sub>`D1-C223` · Day 1, How Search works and where's AI? (Cherry Prommawin) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google described its search results page as an auction system in which the individual results, of different types, all bid for a place on the page; the auction is a metaphor for result types competing for space, not a reference to ads.
  <br><sub>`D3-C302` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Text results are the most common and most prominent result type on Google's results page, whether they are generated by an LLM or not, or enhanced in some other way, Google's speaker said.
  <br><sub>`D3-C303` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs</sub>

- **[Stage]** Which kinds of results Google shows for a query is decided by query understanding, which tries to predict the intent behind the query.
  <br><sub>`D3-C304` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works) · Extends [D3-C004](../../40-sessions/day3/D3-S03-making-sense-of-users-queries.md)</sub>

- **[Stage]** When the query itself names the wanted result type, as 'pictures' does in 'orange pictures' (or a query asking for videos or news), Google can read the intent directly from that word.
  <br><sub>`D3-C305` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery), [In-depth guide to how Google Search works](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/fundamentals/how-search-works)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google said it shows images on the web results page, not only in image search, because from 2005-2006 it saw people appending words such as 'pictures' or 'images' to their queries, which led to the launch of universal search.
  <br><sub>`D3-C306` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · not in Google docs · Used by the glossary term *Universal search*</sub>

- **[Stage]** For an ambiguous query such as 'orange', Google uses historical data: it looks at how users reacted to different kinds of results for previous and similar queries and shows the result types users prefer.
  <br><sub>`D3-C309` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Automatically generating and ranking results](https://www.google.com/search/howsearchworks/how-search-works/ranking-results/)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google uses an abstract drawing of the search results page in its documentation so that the illustration does not go out of date as fast as a screenshot.
  <br><sub>`D3-C313` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)</sub>

- **[Stage]** A text result on Google's results page is made of parts such as the attribution, the title link, the snippet and the site name.
  <br><sub>`D3-C314` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google generates the parts of a text result, such as title link and snippet, from its understanding of the underlying web page, even when the site owner provides nothing extra.
  <br><sub>`D3-C316` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · confirmed by Google docs · [Influencing your title links in search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/title-link), [Control your snippets in search results](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/snippet) · Extends [D2-C724](../../40-sessions/day2/D2-S23-how-does-the-index-look-like.md) · Used by `DEV-HTM-03`</sub>

- **[Stage]** Google can add elements to a text result, such as a 'highly cited' badge or a preferred-source badge.
  <br><sub>`D3-C317` · Day 3, How Search results are born (Gary Illyes, Search Relations) · consistent with Google docs · [Help your readers find your site through preferred sources in Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/preferred-sources) · Extends [D1-C027](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S02-what-s-new-in-the-world-of-search.md)</sub>

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** Google's site names were introduced on mobile results for select languages in October 2022, expanded to desktop in March 2023, and on 7 September 2023 became available in all languages where Google Search is available, on mobile and desktop.
  <br><sub>`D2-C980` · Search Central blog (7 September 2023) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session G: Internationalisation · is the documentation · [Site names on Google Search now available for all languages](https://developers.google.com/search/blog/2023/09/site-names-global-rollout)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's Visual Elements gallery describes a text result as based on the page's textual content, with attribution, title link and snippet; attribution can include the site name, favicon and visible URL, and a rich result typically relies on structured data.
  <br><sub>`D3-C315` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Visual Elements gallery of Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/visual-elements-gallery)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's site name documentation says site names are generated automatically from a site's home page and references to it on the web, and that a site can indicate its preferred name with WebSite structured data on its home page.
  <br><sub>`D3-C336` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 3, How Search results are born · is the documentation · [Provide a site name to Google Search](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/site-names) · Used by `DEV-SDA-15`, the glossary term *Site name*</sub>
